explanation: In Saudi Arabia, beckoning someone with your finger is considered extremely rude and demeaning, as it mimics the gesture used to call a dog or a servant. This action is deeply offensive in Arab culture, where respect and honor are paramount in social interactions. Instead, use an open hand or a subtle nod to signal someone to approach.
local_tip: To call someone politely, extend your right hand with the palm facing down and wave your fingers toward you gently.
regional_note: While the taboo is consistent across the country, older generations and more conservative regions (e.g., Najd) may find it even more offensive than younger, urban Saudis.

also_check.note: Beckoning with the index finger is considered rude and dog-like; use a gentle wave with all fingers together.
This gesture is highly offensive and can be seen as a challenge or insult, especially when directed at someone older.
While common in casual settings, it can be perceived as condescending or aggressive in formal or professional contexts.
